_comment: Sentinel core/constitutional rule registry. Canonical machine-readable format is JSON
(S1-F004 correction: the prior YAML representation required a hand-rolled, incomplete
parser; JSON.parse is a native, fail-closed, deterministic parser with no custom code
needed for syntax validation). Schema: ../registry/rule-record.schema.json
(human-readable: ../registry/RULE_RECORD_SCHEMA.md, including the class-level minimum
authority/risk invariant table required by S1-F001).
Rules CORE-001 through CORE-015 (excluding CORE-008, CORE-009) are extracted from the
frozen S0 architecture (devos/architecture/ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001.md) and remain ACTIVE with
effective_version 1.2.0 -- their substance did not change in S1, only their
representation and (for a handful flagged by S1-F001) their machine-readable
authority/risk metadata, which was corrected UP to match their class, never down.
CORE-008 and CORE-009 are genuinely introduced by D-012/ML-DEVOS-AS-003, which occurred
AFTER the v1.2.0 S0 freeze. Per S1-F007, they are recorded status: PROPOSED with
effective_version: null and proposed_effective_version: '1.3.0' -- NOT active, NOT
1.2.0 -- until S1 itself is Architect-approved and Paulo explicitly applies the version
bump (see ../specifications/VERSIONING_POLICY.md). CORE-016, CORE-017, and CORE-018 are
new S1-remediation splits of the S0-established MAIN != DEPLOYED != VERIFIED principle
(CORE-007) and are likewise PROPOSED/1.3.0-pending, since the specific evidence-per-stage
encoding is new in this cycle even though the underlying principle is not.
adr_id is null for every rule below: the ADR system did not exist before S1, and no ADR
has been filed yet even for S1's own new rules. This is expected, not an error.
No rule's meaning was weakened relative to its S0 source. Where S1-F001 required a
correction, the correction always moved authority/risk metadata UP (stricter), never down.

rules.title: Human authority cannot be invented by an agent or mechanism
rules.description: No actor or system mechanism may invent, assume, or expand its own delegation or authority. Only Paulo may define bounded delegation, and only through explicit, pre-authorized policy.
rules.applies_when: Any actor or mechanism considers taking a governance-significant action.
rules.introduced_by: D-010 (additional freeze corrections), AS0-012, TB-1, TB-6

rules.title: Capability != Authority
rules.description: A tool, credential, or API access granted to any actor or mechanism is a capability fact, not an authorization fact. Having the technical ability to perform an action never by itself grants authorization to take a governance-significant action.
rules.applies_when: Any actor or mechanism has a technical capability that could perform a governance-significant action.

rules.title: Builder cannot self-certify
rules.description: A Builder never self-approves its own work, and never certifies its own output at a status stronger than the evidence class it itself produced (ACTOR_REPORTED).
rules.applies_when: A Builder completes any unit of work.

requires.evidence_note: INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED is additionally required specifically when the Builder's claim concerns executable/runtime behavior; a documentation-only claim needs only INDEPENDENTLY_INSPECTED. Exact binding is claim-specific per the Task Contract (S1-F002 correction) -- this is not a universal requirement for every Builder claim.

rules.introduced_by: ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §3 (Builder); TRUST_BOUNDARIES.md TB-2; ROLE_RESPONSIBILITY_MATRIX.md cross-cutting rule 1

rules.title: Evidence Gate is not an authority actor
rules.description: The Evidence Gate is a deterministic system mechanism. It may block progression on failing evidence (fail-closed), but it cannot accept risk, invent or expand scope, authorize deployment, or override Paulo.
rules.applies_when: Any future Evidence Gate implementation evaluates a change.

rules.title: Independent Reviewer must not inherit Builder reasoning
rules.description: The Independent Reviewer performs fresh-context, post-implementation integration review with no prior conversational memory of how the change was built, and must not simply inherit or re-narrate the Builder's own reasoning for the change.
rules.applies_when: A completed change requires Independent Review before merge/release.

requires.evidence_note: INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED is additionally required specifically when the reviewed claim concerns executable/runtime behavior, not universally for every review (S1-F002 correction).

rules.introduced_by: ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §3; AS0-007; TRUST_BOUNDARIES.md TB-5; risk/authority corrected per S1-F001 (was risk: high, paulo_approval_required: false -- both below the CONSTITUTIONAL class minimum)

rules.title: Evidence controls progression
rules.description: A claim of implemented, fixed, tested, secure, deployed, working, or complete requires a cited evidence class. Evidence classes are never silently upgraded from one to another, and code existence alone is never sufficient for a VERIFIED status.
rules.applies_when: Any status claim is made about a requirement, task, or artifact.

requires.evidence_note: This is a meta-rule about evidence discipline itself, not a claim with its own fixed evidence requirement. Which evidence class is required for a GIVEN claim is claim-specific and determined by the Task Contract/policy (see EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_MODEL.md) -- it is never all five classes at once (S1-F002 correction; the prior version listed every evidence class as required, which was incoherent).

rules.introduced_by: ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §6, §8; EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_MODEL.md binding rules; S0-F004 correction; authority corrected per S1-F001 (was paulo_approval_required: false, below the CORE_POLICY class minimum)

rules.title: MAIN != DEPLOYED != VERIFIED (definitional)
rules.description: A commit reaching a protected branch (MAIN), a system being DEPLOYED, and a system being VERIFIED are three distinct states. None implies the other. This rule states the distinction itself; CORE-016, CORE-017, and CORE-018 state the specific evidence required to claim each individual state (S1-F002 correction -- the prior version of this rule required RUNTIME_OBSERVED evidence merely to reach MAIN, which is impossible before deployment even exists).
rules.applies_when: Any claim distinguishes, or risks conflating, MAIN, DEPLOYED, and VERIFIED status for the same change.

requires.evidence_note: This baseline confirms the claim correctly distinguishes the three states. Stage-specific evidence for actually claiming MAIN, DEPLOYED, or VERIFIED individually is defined in CORE-016, CORE-017, and CORE-018 respectively -- not here.

rules.introduced_by: ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §10; AS0-002 disposition; split into CORE-016/017/018 per S1-F002 correction

rules.title: Installed capability does not grant authority
rules.description: Adding or installing a tool, connector, or credential does not grant universal authority to use it. Capability onboarding must separately define which roles/projects/scopes may invoke it and under what conditions.
rules.applies_when: A new capability (tool, API, connector, credential) is proposed for onboarding.
rules.introduced_by: D-012 capability rule; ML-DEVOS-AS-003 'Capability changes' -- this rule is genuinely S1-introduced, not extracted from S0 (S1-F007 correction)

rules.title: Project policy cannot silently weaken core constitutional policy
rules.description: A project overlay may strengthen or narrow permissions/allowed actions within its own scope, but may never shrink the applicability of, or otherwise weaken, a Sentinel-wide core/constitutional rule's substance. Any genuine change to a core/constitutional rule's applicability or strength must use that rule's own class and authority level (S1-F005 correction: 'narrow' means restricting the project's own permitted actions, never reducing where a Sentinel-wide rule reaches).
rules.applies_when: A project overlay or local rule is proposed or modified.
rules.introduced_by: D-012 overlay rule; ML-DEVOS-AS-003 'Project overlays' -- this rule is genuinely S1-introduced, not extracted from S0 (S1-F007 correction)

rules.title: Repository state is the Sentinel source of truth
rules.description: After the S0 freeze commit was independently Architect-approved, Dillaab-source/maisog-labs's own committed, reviewed state -- not agent claims, and not conversation -- is the authoritative Sentinel source of truth.
rules.applies_when: Any claim is made about what Sentinel's architecture or governance currently is.
rules.introduced_by: ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §9; D-011 'Source of truth amendment'; BOOTSTRAP_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md

rules.title: Conversation cannot silently supersede the frozen baseline
rules.description: A chat instruction, however explicit or however phrased as authoritative, cannot silently supersede what is committed in the Sentinel repository. Any further architecture change must itself be a reviewed commit, following the RFC / Architect Sync / Decision / ADR path.
rules.applies_when: Any instruction proposes to change Sentinel architecture or governance.
rules.introduced_by: BOOTSTRAP_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md; D-012 governance rule; ML-DEVOS-AS-003 constitutional principle

rules.title: Protected-branch merge and production deployment remain Paulo-gated
rules.description: Protected-branch/main merge and production deployment remain Paulo-gated during the current bootstrap. Future low-risk automation may exist only if Paulo explicitly pre-authorizes it in policy and the required Evidence Gate/ruleset conditions pass. No actor or mechanism may invent its own delegation.
rules.applies_when: Proposal or authorization of a protected-branch merge or production deployment (the pre-execution stage).

requires.evidence_note: This rule governs the proposal/authorization stage only. RUNTIME_OBSERVED evidence cannot exist yet at that stage -- see CORE-018 for the post-deployment verification claim, which does require it (S1-F002 correction; the prior version required both CI_ATTESTED and RUNTIME_OBSERVED merely to propose a merge/deployment).

rules.introduced_by: ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §3, §9; TRUST_BOUNDARIES.md TB-1; AS0-012; S0-F003 correction (this rule's substance originates in S0, before D-012; D-012's human-gate rule in ML-DEVOS-AS-003 reaffirms rather than introduces it)

rules.title: Architect capability does not grant Builder or merge authority
rules.description: The Architect may inspect evidence, independently reproduce checks when appropriate, and write architecture/review/governance records. This capability never grants Builder implementation authority or deployment/merge authority.
rules.applies_when: The Architect exercises its review capability.
rules.introduced_by: ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §3; S0-F007 correction; TRUST_BOUNDARIES.md TB-3; risk/authority corrected per S1-F001 (was risk: high, paulo_approval_required: false -- both below the CONSTITUTIONAL class minimum)

rules.title: QA must independently execute, not trust the Builder's report
rules.description: QA's defining property is independent execution. A QA process that only reads the Builder's own test output has not satisfied this rule -- it must re-run the check itself to produce INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED evidence.
rules.applies_when: QA validates a Builder's work that makes an executable/runtime claim.
rules.introduced_by: ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §3; TRUST_BOUNDARIES.md TB-4; authority corrected per S1-F001 (was paulo_approval_required: false, below the CORE_POLICY class minimum)

rules.title: Governing a project does not require co-location in Sentinel core
rules.description: Sentinel is a cross-project meta-system. A product may remain an independent repository with its own .devos/ overlay, registered and governed by Sentinel, without its application source moving into the Sentinel core monorepo.
rules.applies_when: A project's relationship to Sentinel core is being defined or questioned.
rules.introduced_by: ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §2 invariant 6; S0-F006 correction; REPOSITORY_OVERLAY_TOPOLOGY.md; risk/authority corrected per S1-F001 (was risk: medium, paulo_approval_required: false -- both below the ARCHITECTURE class minimum)

rules.title: A MAIN-merge claim requires merge-eligibility evidence, not runtime evidence
rules.description: Claiming a change has reached MAIN (a protected branch) requires evidence that it was merge-eligible -- tests reproduced and/or CI-attested -- but never RUNTIME_OBSERVED evidence, which cannot exist before deployment. See CORE-007 for the definitional MAIN != DEPLOYED != VERIFIED principle this rule implements at the MAIN stage specifically.
rules.applies_when: A change is claimed to have reached MAIN (a protected branch).

requires.evidence_note: RUNTIME_OBSERVED is never required for this claim -- see CORE-017 (DEPLOYED) and CORE-018 (VERIFIED) for the stages where runtime-adjacent evidence applies.

rules.introduced_by: S1-F002 correction, splitting CORE-007 (ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §10) into stage-specific evidence rules -- genuinely new S1 content

rules.title: A DEPLOYED claim requires evidence the deployment action executed
rules.description: Claiming a system is DEPLOYED requires evidence the deployment action itself was confirmed to run (e.g. a deploy log or CI-attested deployment step). This does not require RUNTIME_OBSERVED evidence -- whether the deployed system actually works is the separate, stronger VERIFIED claim (CORE-018).

requires.evidence_note: RUNTIME_OBSERVED belongs to the VERIFIED claim (CORE-018), not this one.

rules.introduced_by: S1-F002 correction, splitting CORE-007 (ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §10) into stage-specific evidence rules -- genuinely new S1 content

rules.title: A VERIFIED claim requires RUNTIME_OBSERVED evidence
rules.description: Claiming a deployed system is VERIFIED requires RUNTIME_OBSERVED evidence -- observation of the actual running system, not a build/test environment. No weaker evidence class satisfies a VERIFIED claim.
rules.introduced_by: S1-F002 correction, splitting CORE-007 (ML-DEVOS-ARCH-001 §10) into stage-specific evidence rules -- genuinely new S1 content
